questions.question: Under a sale offer, Tanvir was offered a 32% discount on the part of the marked price that was paid in cash, but had to add 1.2% on the part of the marked price paid through a credit card. If Tanvir paid 75% of the marked price in cash and the rest through a credit card, what percentage of the marked price was his total final payment?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Discount% on part of MP is 32% 

Credit Card Discount on part of MP is 1.2%

Tanvir paid 75% of the marked price in cash and the rest through a credit card

**Calculations:**

According to the question,

Payment in cash,

Payment = [(100 - 32)/100] × 75/100 × MP

⇒ 68/100 × 75/100 × MP

⇒ (68 × 75)/10000 × MP

⇒ 5100/10000 × MP

⇒ Payement = 0.51MP

Payment in card,

Payment = [(100 + 1.2)/100] × [(100 - 75)/100] × MP

⇒ 101.2/100 × 25/100 × MP

⇒ (101.2 × 25)/10000 × MP

⇒ 2530/10000 × MP

⇒ Payement = 0.235MP

Total Payment = 0.51MP + 0.253 MP = 0.763 MP

Now, Percentage = 0.763MP/ MP × 100 = 76.3%

**∴ His total final payment was 76.3%.**

questions.question: A man purchased a car for Rs. 12 lakh and was insured at 80% of the cost. He sold the car at a 15% loss but had not yet delivered it to the buyer when he met with an accident. After the accident, the car damaged a lot and the insurance company paid 90% of the insured amount. The net difference in the two transactions is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A man purchased a car for price = Rs. 12 lakh

Car was insured at = 80% of the cost of the car

Car was sold at the loss of = 15%

The percentage of the insured amount paid by the insurance company = 90%

**Formula:**

x% of a number = Actual number × (x/100)

**Given:**

SP = 12,00,000 × (85/100) = 10,20,000

Amount paid by the insurance company = 12,00,000 × (80/100) × (90/100) = 8,64,000

∴ Required difference = 10,20,000 - 8,64,000 = 1,56,000 or 1.56 lakhs

questions.question: A person marks his 40 items at 20% above the cost price. He sells 10 items at a 10% discount and 20 items at a 15% discount on the marked price. What is the maximum discount (rounded off) he can offer on the remaining items if he still gets some profit?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Total number of items = 40

MP of the items is more than that of cost price is = 20%

The person sells 10 items at a discount = 10%

He sells 20 items at a discount = 15%

**Formula:**

Discount = MP – SP

Discount % = Discount/MP × 100 

**Calculation:**

Let cost price of each items be Rs. 1

Cost price of 40 items = 1 × 40 = Rs. 40

MP of 40 items = 40 × (120/100) = Rs. 48

Selling price of 10 items = 10 × (120/100) × (90/100) = Rs. 10.8

Selling price of 20 items = 20 × (120/100) × (85/100) = Rs. 20.4

MP of the remaining 10 items = 10 × 120/100 = Rs. 12

Net profit = (12 + 20.4 + 10.8) - Rs. 40 = 43.2 - 40 = Rs. 3.2

If he gives discount Rs. 3.2 on Rs. 12 he gets neither profit nor loss.

Required discount = 3.2/12 × 100 = 26.67%

Now we can say after giving 26% discount he still gets some profit.

questions.question: A shopkeeper normally allows a discount of 10% on the marked price of each article. During a sale season, he decides to give two more discounts, the first being at a rate of 50% of the original and the second at a rate of 40% of the first. What is the percentage rate of the equivalent single discount (correct up to two decimal places)?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Discount percent on the marked price = 10%

Discount percent in the first case = 50% of 10 

Discount percent in the second case = 40% of the first case

**Calculation:**

Let the marked price be Rs 100

⇒ Discount = 10% = 1/10 = (10 - 1)/10 = 9/10

S.P = 9/10 × 100 = 90

Now, Discount percent in the first case = 50% of 10 

⇒ 50/100 × 10 = 5%

And, Discount percent in the second case = 40% of the first case

⇒ 40/100 × 5 = 2%

Now the selling price in season is, 

⇒ 90 × (100 - 5)/100 × (100 - 2)/100

⇒ 90 × 95/100 × 98/100 

⇒ 83.79

Hence the actual discount is, 

⇒ 100 - 83.79 = 16.21

**∴ The percentage rate of the equivalent single discount 16.21%**

questions.question:
A shopkeeper offers the following 3 schemes. Which scheme has the maximum discount percentage?

I. Two successive discount of 20% and 25%

II. Buy 5 get 3 free

III. Buy 5 get 6
questions.solution:
Scheme I. Two successive discounts of 20% and 25%

So, effective discount for scheme I is = 20 + 25 - (20 × 25)/100 = 45 - 5 = 40%

Scheme II. Buy 5 get 3 free

So, effective discount for scheme II is = (Article get free)/(Total articles) × 100 = 3/(5 + 3) × 100 = 37.5%

Scheme III. Buy 5 get 6

So, effective discount for scheme III is = (Article get free)/(Total articles) × 100 = 1/(6 ) × 100 = 16.67%

So, answer is Scheme I.

questions.question: Raj purchased two laptops, first for Rs. 42500 and the second for Rs 36200. He sold first laptop at a profit of 12% and the second laptop at a loss of 12%.What is the overall profit or loss?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

C.P of first laptop = Rs.42500

C.P of second laptop = Rs.36200

**Calculation:**

CP of first laptop = 42500

Thus, SP of first laptop = 42500 × 112/100 = 47600

CP of second laptop = 36200

Thus, SP of second laptop = 36200 × 88/100 = 31856

Total CP of first and second laptop = 42500 + 36200 = 78700

And total SP of first and second laptop = 47600 + 31856 = 79456

Profit = Total SP – Total CP = 79456 – 78700 = 756

**∴ The correct answer is Rs.756.**
